label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 1.74, PHQ-9 depression mean of 1.75, and notably high GAD-7 anxiety mean of 2.17, this group consistently scores above average on all three distress indicators. The combination of extensive screen time and graduate-level education suggests individuals who may be heavily engaged in digital work or social environments yet experience significant emotional isolation and psychological burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Extended daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
Elevated loneliness despite likely digital connectivity
Highest anxiety levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean 2.17)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting compounded distress
tone: Anxious, emotionally burdened, and socially disconnected despite high digital engagement

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They demonstrate strong psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions, with particularly minimal anxiety scores and low depression indicators, suggesting a generally resilient and emotionally stable group.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77), indicating strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33), well below clinical thresholds
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.09), suggesting very low worry or nervousness
Moderate and controlled screen/internet use (1–3 hours daily)
Higher educational attainment, which may serve as a protective factor

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the affective distress patterns typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of emotional resilience or effective coping that buffers against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen/social-media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) suggesting minimal clinical depression
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) indicating limited generalized anxiety
Moderate and controlled digital engagement (1–3 hours daily), possibly reflecting disciplined screen-time habits
Disconnect between social isolation feelings and affective well-being, hinting at internalized coping strategies
tone: Quietly detached yet psychologically stable; socially under-connected but not emotionally overwhelmed
